topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the hallmarks of cancer framework and outlines the lecture objectives regarding how genetic mutations drive tumor phenotypes.

topics.label: Deregulated growth signaling and proliferative autonomy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how oncogenic mutations in key signaling cascades confer growth signal autonomy and override growth-inhibitory controls.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how differentiation arrest contributes to tumor development in both hematopoietic malignancies and intestinal carcinomas.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis through p53 and Bcl-2 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and the dysregulation of pro- and anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomeres, and senescence bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells achieve replicative immortality by overcoming telomere-driven senescence and p53-mediated stress checkpoints.

topics.label: Complex hallmarks and cancer metabolic rewiring
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics transition to complex tumor phenotypes and examine how metabolic reprogramming, the Warburg effect, and oncometabolites sustain cancer cell growth.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and vascularization
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the angiogenic switch and how tumors stimulate new blood vessel formation to overcome oxygen and nutrient diffusion limits.

topics.label: Mechanisms, detection, and genomics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the multi-step metastatic cascade, circulating tumor cell monitoring, seed-and-soil interactions, and the genomic features of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with a summary of the hallmarks of cancer and references for further reading.
